newsitem.title: UK: Statoil ceo says may complete asset swaps in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Statoil ceo says may complete asset swaps in Q2.

text.p: Norway's state oil company, Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap AS (Statoil), could complete a massive series of asset swaps as early as May as part of a refocussing of its upstream activity, Statoil president and chief executive officer Harald Norvik said Thursday.

"I think the end of this story will probably be in the second quarter, maybe late in the second quarter," Norvik told Reuters after addressing the Norwegian British Chamber of Commerce on Statoil's future strategy.

Norvik said there had been a "very encouraging" number of responses from companies interested in swapping assets on the Norwegian Continental Shelf, in British waters and in the Gulf of Mexico, for equity Statoil wishes to offload.

The aim of refocussing its upstream portfolio at home and abroad is a central part of Statoil's strategy to double oil and gas production by 2005 to one million barrels per day (bpd) of oil equivalent, including 300,000 bpd from overseas.
Norvik said it was possible Statoil may adopt a piece-meal approach to the swaps, allowing early conclusion of negotiations with some partners.
"It might be that we can take them in sequences in which case we may be able to take some decisions on swaps earlier than in May/June, but we will probably need the time," he told Reuters.

Industry consultants Wood Mackenzie said earlier this month Statoil's plans to concentrate its Norwegian activities on five core areas which hold the bulk of its reserves and which account for about 90 percent of its equity crude production, could lead to the largest North Sea asset sale of recent years.

"The combined base asset value of the commercial reserves which are on offer is in excess of $600 million. Significant additional value will also be attributable to the exploration acreage which is being made available," Wood Mackenzie said in a report.
Norvik was unwilling to provide details of the companies interested in swapping assets, but he confirmed that some U.K. acreage had been offered.
Wood Mackenzie said Enterprise Oil, Amerada Hess, British Petroleum and Conoco, a unit of Du Pont, which all operate in both Norwegian and British waters, would be likely counterparties for Statoil.
